messages:
customer_alex: hey team — since ~09:40 PT our dedicated pool rp-789 started returning 429s and tails of p95/p99 latency jumped to ~3s. We bought reserved capacity for 10k qps so shouldn't be hitting caps. Example req id: rq_0a1b2c3d. Billing also shows an unexpected spike. Can someone triage?
support_jess: sorry about that — passing to infra. Can you paste one full X-Redwood-Request-Id header value + the exact pool id and account id? Also which region?
customer_alex: pool=rp-789, acct=12345, region=us-west-2, req id rq_0a1b2c3d. Seen 429s from 09:40-09:55. quick repro curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Pool-ID: rp-789' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` — returns 429 intermittently.
quota-bot: Alert: reserved_pool_saturation rp-789 crossed 90% threshold at 2025-11-12T09:42:10Z; tokens exhausted on 3/8 shards.
eng_tom: looking into telemetry now. Preliminary: aggregate tokens look ok but a few shards went to zero. Can you confirm if the client traffic comes from a small set of source IPs? affinity could cause hot-shard exhaustion. @sre_maria can you pull the rate-limiter mapping?
sre_maria: pulled config: rp-789 -> rate_limit=200 qps per shard, burst=1000 tokens, shards=8. BUT production still has an older rate-limiter version (rlv1) with a global soft-cap of 1300 rps that can be enforced per node. Snippet from 429 response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: 1300/1300
x-rw-pool-id: rp-789
x-rw-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
```
This smells like shard imbalance + local node cap hitting even though pool aggregate should have spare capacity.
eng_tom: known edge from last week's rollout: shard-affinity pins heavy clients to the same shard. Repro steps I use:
1) run a steady rps from same source to pin affinity
2) watch per-shard tokens drop and per-node cap trigger
Example load tool: `hey --concurrency 200 --rps 800 -H 'X-Pool-ID: rp-789' -H 'X-Client-IP: 10.0.0.5' POST /v1/generate`
I'll try to reproduce in canary.
support_jess: immediate workarounds: route a subset of traffic to a fallback pool or add client-side jitter across IPs to spread shards. We can also temporarily increase burst_tokens for rp-789. Which do you prefer?
customer_alex: please increase burst_tokens if safe. We need headroom for the next 30m. Also why did billing spike? We thought reserved capacity covered us.
billing-bot: FYI: any usage above the reserved commit is billed at PAYG rates. We saw overflow to shared capacity between 09:43-09:50 which caused extra usage. I've flagged a billing review and started a credit request.
sre_maria: recommended plan: short-term -> bump burst_tokens to 2000 for rp-789 and monitor; medium-term -> roll back/adjust the rlv1 rollout to remove the global hard-cap or implement affinity smoothing. I'll draft a PR for the smoother affinity algorithm and a canary plan + rollback steps.
eng_tom: applying burst bump now via internal CLI: `redwoodctl pools update rp-789 --burst-tokens 2000` — I'll run a controlled canary and watch per-shard fill.
support_jess: applied burst bump and opened a billing credit ticket, cc finance. Metrics: 429 rate dropped to near zero within 2 minutes, p95 latency improved.
customer_alex: confirmed — errors reduced and latency looks back to normal. Thanks. Please send a follow-up PM with permanent fix ETA.
support_jess: will follow up with a postmortem and a short SLA alignment note (we'll document shard-affinity caveat). Closing once PR merged. :thumbsup:
